open_points.subject: prove_version phase 4 guard membership
open_points.other_text: - prove_version: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run nine phases in this fixed order and return at the first failing check, items within a phase in that phase's order and conditions of one item in the order listed: 1 nodes by node_id, a function node names a contract version that read_contract_version finds and an operation node names a binding that read_binding finds with status accepted; 2 constants by to_node then to_port, the port exists and is an input port of a node, never a flow output, of value carriage, the constant's declared value_schema equals the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema text for a one port, the canonical array schema with it as items for a many port) — composition already refused a value that does not fit its declared schema, so no separate value check runs here; 3 edges in edge order, both ports exist with the right direction, carry equal value_schema text, the same carriage and for files the same media type, a flow endpoint port being value carriage; 4 guards in edge order, the guard port is an output of one cardinality of the edge's source node, that node has no map_over, its schema is a closed set with enum or const, and the guard value is a member: guard_value is canonical JSON text, and it is a member when it equals, as text, the canonical JSON (canonical_bytes) of one enum member or of the const.
open_points.question: Must canonical_bytes return canonical JSON text instead of bytes, or must the guard rule specify decoding its bytes (or encoding guard_value) before comparison?
